{{Short description|Chinese mathematician (1938–2020)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Ding (surname)|Ding]]|lang=Chinese}}
'''Ding Xieping''' ({{zh|s=丁协平}}; 16 April 1938 – 4 January 2020) was a Chinese mathematician and a professor at [[Sichuan Normal University]]. He served as Director of the Institute of Mathematics at the university.

== Biography ==
Ding was born on 16 April 1938 in [[Zigong]], [[Sichuan]], Republic of China.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://news.sicnu.edu.cn/details/40_25515|title=著名数学家丁协平教授|last=Zhang Cha 张叉|date=2020-01-04|website=Sichuan Normal University|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114012639/http://news.sicnu.edu.cn/details/40_25515 |archive-date=2020-01-14 |access-date=2020-01-14}}</ref> After graduating from [[Sichuan University]] in 1961, he taught as an assistant professor at the Department of Mathematics of the former Chengdu University (now [[Southwestern University of Finance and Economics]]).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_5436984|title=82岁著名数学家、四川师范大学教授丁协平逝世|last=Yue|first=Huairang|date=2020-01-05|website=The Paper|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114012634/https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_5436984 |archive-date=2020-01-14 |access-date=2020-01-14}}</ref>

In 1964, Ding transferred to [[Sichuan Normal University]], where he taught until his retirement in 2010. He served as Director of the university's Institute of Mathematics.<ref name=":0" /> His research focus was [[nonlinear analysis]] and applications. Starting in 1979, he published more than 360 research papers, including 160 on [[Science Citation Index]] (SCI) journals.<ref name=":0" /> In 1999 and 2000, he was China's most prolific authors of papers on SCI journals in the field of mathematics.<ref name=":1" />

He was named a National Outstanding Scientist in 1986 and was awarded a special pension for distinguished scholars by the [[State Council of the People's Republic of China]]. He was named a National Outstanding Teacher in 2001.<ref name=":1" />

Ding died on 4 January 2020, aged 81.<ref name=":0" />
